claims.text: Zhu et al. (2024) proposed CoST (Contrastive Quantization-based Semantic Tokenization), highlighting that traditional vector quantization with reconstruction loss fails to capture neighborhood relationships vital for recommendation.
Qu et al. (2024) developed TokenRec with a Masked Vector-Quantized (MQ) Tokenizer that quantizes masked user/item representations from collaborative filtering into discrete tokens.
Zheng et al. (2023) presented LC-Rec, addressing the semantic gap between LLMs and recommender systems through two major contributions:
Tan et al. (2024) introduced IDGen, representing items as unique, concise, semantically rich textual IDs using human language tokens.

Liu et al. (2024) extended generative recommendation to multimodal settings with MMGRec, addressing limitations of the embed-and-retrieve paradigm (inference cost, interaction modeling, false-negatives).
Deng et al. (2025) proposed OneRec, the first end-to-end generative model unifying retrieve and rank stages, replacing cascaded learning frameworks.

Zheng et al. (2023) designed specially tuned tasks enforcing LLMs to integrate language and collaborative semantics through learned item indices, moving beyond simple instruction following to deep semantic integration.
Deng et al. (2025) customized DPO for recommendation by designing a reward model to simulate user generation and a specialized sampling strategy addressing the single-opportunity constraint.

Tan et al. (2024) aligned LLMs with recommendation needs through textual ID learning, decoupling user history from original datasets and expressing it in natural language, suggesting foundational model potential.

Hou et al. (2024) introduced BLaIR, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs as semantic encoders in recommendation, addressing the gap between general-purpose embedding benchmarks (e.g., MTEB) and recommendation-specific requirements.
Zhu et al. (2024) (CoST) demonstrated that contrastive quantization capturing item relationships significantly outperforms reconstruction-only objectives.
Only OneRec (Deng et al., 2025) reports real-world deployment results, achieving 1.6% watch-time improvement at Kuaishou.
